exact_cover_quotes.quote: Confirmed 2026-09-28: files left behind are not a leak, and need no extra cleanup machinery, when they are bounded by a fixed amount, grow only with a rare and explicit user action (such as switching the release download source), or are removed by the next attempt at the same operation or by the next start of the process that owns them. As with retained supervisor metadata, the line is accumulation without bound over time during ordinary operation.

The local security boundary is the Unix account on a particular host. Processes the user runs on the target host, including same-account processes that can reach Farhelm's terminal hosts (the processes that keep its terminals), are trusted by this threat model. Farhelm does not provide strong same-account isolation against deliberate interference with agents or those terminal hosts, and session credentials do not provide same-account containment.
